sections.text: A HashMap stores values under keys, so you can look things up by name instead of by position. Bring it in with use.
stock["pears"] reads a value directly, but it panics (stops the program) if the key is missing. Use it only when you know the key is there; otherwise use get.
get returns an Option because the key might be missing. The entry API inserts a default the first time it sees a key, which is perfect for counting:

entry(word).or_insert(0) inserts 0 if the word is new, then gives back a mutable reference (&mut) to the count stored in the map. The * in front follows that reference, so += 1 changes the count inside the map, just like *n in the Mutable references lesson. get is different: it returns an Option holding a reference to the value, so a fallback has to be a reference too, as in unwrap_or(&0). get also takes a reference to the key. A literal like "apples" is already a reference (&str), so stock.get("apples") needs no &, but a char key needs one: counts.get(&'a').

You can loop over all the keys. The order isn't guaranteed, so sort them if you need a fixed order. Below, ages.keys() hands out each key in turn and .collect() gathers them into a new Vec. Writing Vec<_> asks for a Vec and lets Rust work out the item type itself (here, references to the names). Unit 8 covers iterators and collect.
A HashMap is like a dictionary: you look up a word (the key) to find its meaning (the value).
Keys need Eq + Hash. Use BTreeMap from the same module when you want keys kept in sorted order.

exercise.prompt: Finish count_letters: use the entry API to count how many times each letter appears in word. For "banana", main prints the count for 'a'. It should print: 3

tests.label: a letter that is not there has no entry
a word a hard-coded answer would not match

hints: For each letter you need to either start a count or add 1 to the existing one. The entry API does this.
counts.entry(c).or_insert(0) gives back a mutable reference to the count. Put * in front of it to follow the reference, then add 1 with += 1.
